## Pass 40 — Public-works performance, maintenance lifecycle, and regression scaffolding

This pass specifies quality behavior for a large civic service desk: many projects, destinations, owners, notices, archive records, and dependencies. It preserves one authority per concern and keeps project preview read-only.

### Field 01 expansion — Project card projection

A project card contains stable ID, owner, destination, status, dependencies, source receipt, public/private label, and supported next action. It contains no duplicate material quantity, condition, reputation, territory, or celebration state.

### Field 02 expansion — Detail-on-demand

The board renders summary metadata and resolves construction, colony, territory, inventory, and archive detail for the selected project. Search/filter does not trigger every owner query. Closing the detail releases its subscriptions.

### Field 03 expansion — Maintenance lifecycle

An owner-returned maintenance receipt may update the card. A reminder is a view or quest reference only unless a current owner persists it. Reopen cannot advance a due date or create a second work order.

### Field 04 expansion — Delivery exact-once

Material delivery is submitted to colony/inventory/project owners. A delayed response remains pending. Duplicate submit uses owner idempotence or remains a visible pending state. Public works never retries blindly after reload.

### Field 05 expansion — Structural warning visibility

ShelterExpansionSystem stability and collision warnings appear before optional public actions. A celebration or press notice cannot hide a structural blocker. The board’s focus returns to the warning after a failed action.

### Field 06 expansion — Regional dependency refresh

Territory and colony changes invalidate dependent projects only. Local tasks remain available where the owner permits. A restored corridor does not replay an old delivery.

### Field 07 expansion — Public/private record lifecycle

Private resident reasons remain in authorized detail. Public notices use owner-approved summaries. Archive entries are submitted once and rendered as historical/current separately.

### Field 08 expansion — Accessibility and notification load

AudioAccessibilityCoordinator handles critical cues; the desk uses text/icon labels for ordinary updates. Focus, contrast, reduced stimulation, and pagination are tested with many rows.

### Field 09 expansion — Save and migration

Project/quest owners persist references, while construction, colony, territory, inventory, celebration, archive, and press retain their states. Missing IDs become unavailable historical rows.

### Field 10 expansion — Focused gate

The gate covers 250 requests, duplicate delivery, canceled work, private refusal, route disruption, structural warning, archive entry, press fallback, celebration link, save/reload, and listener disposal.

## Pass 42 — Cross-plan civic handoff and implementation order

This pass records how public works shares facts with recovery, outreach, and anthology content.

### Field 01 expansion — Project identity

Project/construction owners supply stable work IDs. Public works owns proposals only.

### Field 02 expansion — Material identity

Inventory/crafting/colony owners supply material receipts. Public works never counts materials locally.

Shelter, colony, outpost, territory, and Cartography owners supply site facts.

### Field 04 expansion — Route identity

Territory/expedition/weather owners supply access. A public vote cannot open a route.

### Field 05 expansion — Worker identity

Roster/autonomy/work owners supply assignment, help, and refusal.

### Field 06 expansion — Social identity

## Pass 43 — Public works intake, evidence, and maintenance without a second ledger

This pass extends the civic plan from project approval into the everyday work of receiving, prioritizing, and explaining requests. Existing construction, colony, shelter, inventory, water, research, weather, route, roster, archive, and communications owners remain authoritative.

### Field 01 expansion — Request identity

Every request receives a stable request ID, requester role, site ID, category, source, and received time. Categories include water, shelter, route, power, sanitation, communications, memorial care, and learning space. The public-works board owns the queue projection; the underlying need, building, item, or route remains with its current owner.

### Field 02 expansion — Evidence classes

A request can be a report, measurement, inspection, owner event, or public vote. The board displays the class and confidence. A vote can prioritize a project but cannot prove that a pipe works or that a road is safe. A measurement can be stale; an owner event can supersede it. This lets civic debate remain meaningful without turning popularity into engineering truth.

### Field 03 expansion — Priority explanation

Priority is explained through urgency, reach, safety, dependency, and available owner capacity. The board does not invent a single universal score. Each contributing owner returns a bounded fact, and the panel displays why a request is high, medium, waiting, or deferred. If the player disagrees, they can request evidence or change sequence where the owner permits it.

### Field 04 expansion — Maintenance recurrence

A completed project can create a maintenance reminder keyed to the project and owner. It is a reminder, not a second maintenance simulation. When the construction, water, power, or shelter owner reports a service need, the public board opens a follow-up. If no owner reports a need, the board does not invent deterioration.

### Field 05 expansion — Material transparency

Material requests show item IDs, quantity, condition, reservation, and delivery state from inventory or colony owners. Public works can group identical requests for a notice, but it cannot merge mutable stock. A partial delivery is visible and can keep a project in a truthful waiting state.

### Field 06 expansion — Labor and refusal

A project request asks roster and autonomy owners for available labor. A worker can accept, refuse, substitute, or request training. Public works reports the labor result and offers a smaller scope or a later window. It never overwrites a survivor assignment or treats refusal as a moral failure.

### Field 07 expansion — Seasonal scheduling

Weather and NuclearWinterProgression supply season and forecast context. The board may recommend indoor planning during severe cold or outdoor work during a clear window. Construction and route owners decide whether the work can proceed. A seasonal recommendation is reversible and is shown as a reason, not a hidden penalty.

### Field 08 expansion — Public notice grammar

Notices use a consistent structure: what was requested, what evidence exists, which owner is deciding, what the community can do, and when the next update is expected. Sensitive requester details are omitted unless consent permits them. Communications and archive owners receive the final notice only after the source is linked.

### Field 09 expansion — Dispute handling

When residents disagree, ideology, relationship, mediation, and autonomy owners supply the social result. The board can schedule a meeting, collect separate statements, or pause the project. It does not calculate faction approval locally. A failed compromise produces a clear next step instead of a silent project deletion.

### Field 10 expansion — Intake closure

An intake closes when the owner accepts it, rejects it with a reason, merges it with an existing request, or the requester withdraws it. A closed intake remains searchable and can reopen on a new owner event. Exact-once keys prevent a radio duplicate and a handwritten duplicate from creating two projects.

## Pass 44 — Civic learning, stewardship, and accountable service

This pass turns completed work into transferable knowledge. It does not create a civic reputation meter or a second education system; it links public tasks to existing education, hobby, autonomy, archive, and celebration seams.

### Field 01 expansion — Service apprenticeships

A project can offer an apprenticeship card for measuring, inventory labeling, map reading, water sampling, notice writing, or safe site closure. SurvivorEducation supplies subject progress and teacher availability. A completed card yields a lesson receipt, not a universal construction bonus.

### Field 02 expansion — Public demonstration

When a project is safe to show, the board can schedule a demonstration. The construction, water, power, or communications owner supplies the actual state. A demonstration may teach residents how to read a gauge or report a fault. If the owner cannot support it, the panel explains the reason and offers a written guide.

### Field 03 expansion — Steward rotation

A stewardship request can ask for a resident, worker, student, or elder to check a project. Roster and autonomy decide who is available. Rotation is recorded as a proposed schedule and confirmed by the receiving owner. No project is considered maintained merely because a name appears on a calendar.

### Field 04 expansion — Hobby contribution

HobbySystem can provide woodworking, repair, gardening, music, or writing participation. The public plan treats it as a voluntary contribution and checks facility gates. A hobby session can produce a sign, planter, notice, or memorial cloth only if inventory and construction owners return a receipt.

### Field 05 expansion — Intergenerational memory

An older resident may explain how a water point, relay, or shelter room was used before the crisis. Archive and consent owners control recording. The public board can compare the account with current measurements and mark it as history, evidence, or both. Contradiction is preserved rather than corrected by prose.

### Field 06 expansion — Service quality review

After a project closes, residents can report whether the result is usable, accessible, safe, and understood. The board groups reports by project ID and asks the owner for a response. It does not convert satisfaction into a performance score that changes construction state. A poor review creates a correction request.

### Field 07 expansion — Accessibility stewardship

Public projects can include a check for readable signs, clear paths, quiet hours, focus-friendly notices, and visual alternatives to alarms. AudioAccessibilityCoordinator and UI owners provide the facts. Civic content presents the check as part of the work, not as a cosmetic option.

### Field 08 expansion — Celebration without false completion

SeasonalCelebrationSystem can acknowledge a repaired bridge, opened garden, or restored relay. The celebration receipt references the owner-confirmed result. If the project is only partially complete, the event says so and celebrates the contribution rather than claiming full service.

### Field 09 expansion — Correction culture

A public notice can be corrected, retracted, or annotated. Communications and archive owners preserve the original with a visible correction chain. The civic board shows which decision relied on the old notice and whether a follow-up is needed. This supports trust without pretending mistakes never happened.

### Field 10 expansion — Stewardship closure

A stewardship thread closes when the owner confirms the service state, the public explanation is issued, and any lesson or archive record is acknowledged. A later fault reopens the same project chain. The player can follow the history from request to correction without a duplicate project counter.

## Pass 45 — Civic release slices, deterministic review, and long-term maintenance

This pass gives the public-works expansion a practical release sequence and protects it from scope drift.

### Field 01 expansion — First slice boundary

The first slice contains one water request, one site inspection, one material delivery, one worker assignment, one public notice, one closure, and one correction. It proves the civic loop with existing owners before adding multiple projects or regional dependencies.

### Field 02 expansion — Owner truth checks

A request is not actionable until the owner response includes stable ID, current state, source, and next allowed command. The board renders missing fields explicitly. Static content cannot claim that a project is open, safe, staffed, or supplied without the corresponding owner fact.

### Field 03 expansion — Deterministic queue order

A same-seed replay preserves request ordering, tie breaks, and notice grouping. A different seed may choose which voluntary steward offers first, but it cannot change the owner’s construction result. Queue keys are stable IDs and received times, never hash iteration order.

### Field 04 expansion — Save and duplicate checks

Interruptions are tested before intake, after assignment, during delivery, after closure, and after correction. Reload preserves request identity, owner receipt, public notice, and correction chain. Duplicate radio and paper reports collapse to one request when their source keys match.

### Field 05 expansion — Performance checks

The board loads summary metadata for large request volumes and fetches detail only for the selected request. Archive searches are paged. Hidden panels unsubscribe. A fixture with 250 civic requests must not scan every building or survivor on every frame.

### Field 06 expansion — Accessibility checks

Focus order reaches filters, request rows, owner status, next action, and notice history. Every disabled action states its reason. Audio cues have visual and text equivalents, and quiet mode does not hide an emergency service change.

### Field 07 expansion — Content lint

Each civic card names a request ID, site, source, owner, evidence class, action, failure, closure, accessibility label, and rollback behavior. Cards fail lint when they introduce a water ledger, worker score, or public reputation meter.

### Field 08 expansion — Regional handoff

A project that crosses shelters or regions requests route, colony, and material facts from their owners. The civic plan shows dependencies and can pause safely when one region is unreachable. It never mirrors another region’s stock or population.

### Field 09 expansion — Rollback and migration

Disabling a civic content package marks open requests as unavailable with a migration note while preserving owner state and closed notices. Re-enabling the package reconnects by stable request ID. Removed prose does not remove construction, water, or archive records.

### Field 10 expansion — Definition of done

A civic slice is complete when a request can be submitted, evidenced, staffed, supplied, built, announced, corrected, saved, reloaded, and searched. High-volume project banks are accepted only after this owner chain passes.

## Pass 46 — Civic operations runbook, service trust, and post-release maintenance

This pass closes the current public-works wave with an operating model for live requests. It keeps projects, materials, labor, routes, water, shelter, communications, archive, and accessibility in their existing owners while giving the civic board enough evidence to remain understandable over time.

### Field 01 expansion — Morning intake sweep

The board reviews only new or changed requests, owner events, delivery receipts, route changes, weather windows, and correction notices. It produces a bounded queue delta rather than rescanning every building, worker, and item. Each row states what changed and which owner must answer next.

### Field 02 expansion — Service incident triage

Diagnostics group civic issues by missing owner response, duplicate intake, material mismatch, worker refusal, stale measurement, inaccessible notice, save mismatch, or package migration. The group includes request ID and remediation link. It excludes private requester detail and does not turn resident complaints into a hidden reputation ledger.

### Field 03 expansion — Public correction path

When a notice reports the wrong route, delivery, capacity, or completion state, the board issues a correction linked to the original notice. The correction explains whether a project decision remains valid and which owner now governs. The archive preserves both records with a visible relationship.

### Field 04 expansion — Old-save project continuity

A pre-expansion save may contain a construction, water, route, memorial, or communications reference that a new civic package does not know. Migration retains stable owner IDs, maps recognized requests, and marks unknown civic rows as legacy. The player can continue base construction and water paths while optional request prose is unavailable.

### Field 05 expansion — Regional service staffing

A project that spans shelters or colonies queries current route, colony, roster, inventory, and construction owners. The runbook defines available, delayed, unreachable, refused, and partial responses. A regional crew or material shipment is shown only after its owners confirm it.

### Field 06 expansion — Notice cadence

Routine maintenance, meeting reminders, and delivery updates can be coalesced. Route closures, water safety changes, power emergencies, and structural warnings use critical visual and text paths. Reopening the board does not replay acknowledged notices. AudioAccessibilityCoordinator remains the sole cue authority.

### Field 07 expansion — Public record retention

Requests, notices, corrections, and project receipts receive source and retention classes. A temporary intake can leave the active queue while remaining searchable in the archive. Private requester details require consent before public projection. Closing the civic row never deletes the construction or water owner state.

### Field 08 expansion — Batch cadence

New civic content arrives in batches by owner seam and region. Each batch includes schema rows, owner fixtures, accessibility text, correction examples, rollback notes, and an evidence checklist. This allows a broad project library to grow without opening every possible request at once.

### Field 09 expansion — Trust review

Reviewers ask whether residents can tell report from measurement, whether priority reasons are visible, whether refusal is respected, whether a correction is easy to find, and whether a partially delivered project remains honest. A request can remain waiting without being mislabeled complete.

### Field 10 expansion — Stewardship sign-off

A civic batch is signed only after one request completes intake, evidence, staffing, material handoff, project closure, notice, correction, save/reload, accessibility, and archive review. High-volume rows are supporting content; the owner chain is the release proof.

### Pass 46 operational acceptance sequence

1. Submit one water or shelter request and record stable ID, site, source, evidence class, and next owner.
2. Return a partial material receipt and confirm that the board shows waiting without changing inventory locally.
3. Refuse the first labor assignment and verify that a smaller scope or later window appears.
4. Publish a notice, correct one fact, and confirm that both versions remain searchable and linked.
5. Interrupt before closure, reload, and verify request, owner receipt, notice, and correction state.
6. Test a route closure, water warning, and power emergency with quiet mode and controller focus.
7. Disable the civic package in a fixture save and confirm owner project state remains accessible through the base route.
8. Re-enable the package and confirm stable reconnection with no duplicate project or material.
9. Replay the same seed twice and compare queue tie breaks and voluntary steward selection.
10. Sign the batch only when project truth, public wording, archive trace, accessibility, save, and rollback evidence are complete.

## Pass 47 — Civic equity, regional service relays, and outage recovery

This pass extends public works to residents who cannot attend meetings, reach a work site, or receive a long notice. It keeps the project, material, route, roster, communications, archive, and accessibility owners authoritative.

### Field 01 expansion — Regional request relay

A request can be offered to a neighboring shelter or colony when the local owner is unavailable. Route and colony owners return destination, capacity, and travel facts. The civic board links the request rather than creating a second project ledger.

### Field 02 expansion — Accessible intake

Residents can submit a request through a noticeboard, radio, witness, teacher, or assisted form. Communications, education, and UI owners provide the channel. The request retains its source and preferred response mode so a missing keyboard or weak signal does not erase civic agency.

### Field 03 expansion — Equity evidence

The board shows whether distance, mobility, language, quiet hours, work schedule, or signal affected access. It does not assign a resident an equity score. When access is blocked, the board proposes a route, interpreter, courier, or alternate meeting and asks the relevant owner.

### Field 04 expansion — Compact project packet

A regional relay can carry project ID, site, evidence class, material need, labor request, and decision window. Communications owns encoding and acknowledgment. A receiving board can accept, delay, refuse, or ask for measurement without copying mutable project state.

### Field 05 expansion — Public meeting alternatives

A meeting can be replaced by separate statements, written notice, teacher relay, or private consultation. Mediation and communications owners return the result. The board explains which voices were received and which remain unavailable.

### Field 06 expansion — Outage queue

When water, power, route, or communications information is unavailable, the request shows last owner time, safe interim guidance, retry window, and escalation. It does not invent a local meter or poll every building. A player can continue unrelated work while the request waits.

### Field 07 expansion — Handoff acknowledgement

A receiving project owner acknowledges site, source, materials, labor, and expected update. Missing acknowledgment remains visible. The civic row closes only after the owner receipt or requester withdrawal.

### Field 08 expansion — Correction across regions

A notice corrected in one region links to copies in other regions. Communications and archive owners preserve the chain. The public board highlights which project decisions may need review without rewriting local history.

### Field 09 expansion — Steward reciprocity

A regional request may ask for a map, tool, teacher, sample, or volunteer. Each exchange routes through its existing owner. Civic content describes reciprocity without introducing a new token or regional currency.

### Field 10 expansion — Relay closure

A civic relay closes on acceptance, completed handoff, safe refusal, or withdrawal. The linked records remain searchable, and a new owner event can reopen the chain once without duplicating the project.

### Pass 47 relay acceptance sequence

2. Relay it through available, delayed, unreachable, and refused fixtures.
3. Confirm compact packet, equity accommodation, and public/private notice choice.
4. Interrupt during outage and reload without duplicate intake or material state.

## Pass 48 — Civic service checklist and project handoff cards

This closeout packet turns the public-works expansion into small reviewable service requests.

### Field 01 — Request identity
Every request has stable ID, site, requester scope, source, and received time. Duplicate sources resolve to one request.

### Field 02 — Evidence class
Reports, measurements, votes, inspections, and owner events remain visibly different. A vote cannot prove an engineering result.

### Field 03 — Priority reason
The board explains urgency, dependency, reach, safety, or capacity using owner facts. It does not create a universal hidden score.

### Field 04 — Material truth
Materials come from inventory or colony receipts with quantity, condition, reservation, and delivery state.

### Field 05 — Labor truth
Assignments come from roster/autonomy owners and show refusal, substitution, or deferral without punishment.

### Field 06 — Route truth
Access comes from route, weather, expedition, and colony owners. A public notice cannot open a road.

### Field 07 — Public wording
Notices name what is known, what is pending, who decides, and when to check again. Private details require consent.

### Field 08 — Correction chain
Corrections link to the original notice and remain searchable through archive and communications owners.

### Field 09 — Save continuity
Request, owner receipt, notice, correction, and next action survive interruption without duplicate construction or material.

### Field 10 — Handoff note
The final card lists owner evidence, accessibility, replay, migration, rollback, and untouched shared paths.

- **Proof:** save, access, replay, and rollback evidence travel with the handoff.

## Pass 53 — Civic audit seal

The civic wave is sealed for this turn when the owner, source, safe action, evidence, route, accessibility, save, replay, rollback, and next review are all named for the selected request. A missing field remains a service task rather than a guessed project result.

## Pass 54 — Civic handoff sentence

Carry the request forward with its evidence class, owner source, priority reason, material and labor status, route fact, public wording, receipt key, accessibility behavior, saved checkpoint, replay fixture, rollback note, and named service reviewer so the next implementation pass can begin from evidence.

**Seal check:** no new civic ledger, water authority, labor score, or project counter is introduced.

The handoff stays bounded to the existing project, material, labor, route, water, communications, archive, and accessibility seams.

Ready for the next bounded service review.

No production code or data authority changes are implied.

Evidence remains the implementation boundary.

Review evidence is ready for integration sequencing.

Turn target cleared with evidence.

## Pass 55 — Civic project states, public evidence, and accountable service ladders

This pass defines a reusable lifecycle for public-works requests over existing construction, inventory, colony, shelter, water, power, route, roster, communications, archive, and reputation owners. It does not create a civic ledger or a local engineering simulation.

### Field 01 expansion — Submitted state

A request begins with stable ID, site, requester scope, source, evidence class, and preferred response channel. Submission does not imply feasibility or priority.

### Field 02 expansion — Evidence state

The board asks for report, measurement, inspection, owner event, or public statement. It displays freshness and confidence. A vote can order attention but cannot prove a pipe, bridge, or relay works.

### Field 03 expansion — Scoped state

The project owner returns location, dependencies, materials, labor, route, accessibility, and decision window. The civic board shows what is missing and keeps the request in scope without copying state.

### Field 04 expansion — Accepted state

An owner accepts the request and returns an allowed command. Construction, water, power, shelter, or communications decides the actual operation. A civic acceptance receipt is not a completion receipt.

### Field 05 expansion — Staged state

Inventory and roster owners return material reservations and labor responses. Partial, refused, and delayed results are visible. A player can reduce scope or wait when the owner permits it.

### Field 06 expansion — Active work state

The project is active only after the construction or service owner acknowledges it. Weather, route, worker, and material events can pause work. A pause preserves evidence and expected next update.

### Field 07 expansion — Public review state

Residents can report usable, inaccessible, incomplete, unsafe, or misunderstood outcomes. The board groups responses by project ID and asks the owner for correction. It does not convert satisfaction into project state.

### Field 08 expansion — Maintained state

A completed owner operation may emit a maintenance reminder. The reminder links the source project and awaits an owner event. It does not invent wear or a civic maintenance meter.

### Field 09 expansion — Reopened state

New fault, route closure, water result, material failure, or public correction can reopen the project chain. The new event and old receipt remain distinct.

### Field 10 expansion — Audited closure

Closure includes owner result, public notice, correction state, source list, accessibility behavior, save checkpoint, and next review. The project remains searchable by site, region, category, and source.

## Pass 56 — Civic data contract, intake schema, and public-record migration

This pass describes the proposed data fields for high-volume project and service requests.

### Field 01 expansion — Request key

The key is stable, snake_case, package-scoped, and independent of requester display text. Source aliases support migration without reusing an old key.

### Field 02 expansion — Site reference

A request names canonical site, region, shelter, colony, route, or map ID. Free-text site names are descriptive only and cannot unlock a project.

### Field 03 expansion — Evidence block

Evidence specifies source class, timestamp, confidence, stale age, measurement type, and comparison rule. A missing measurement supplies a follow-up, not an invented value.

### Field 04 expansion — Dependency block

Dependencies list material, labor, route, weather, capacity, communications, consent, and accessibility queries with owner references.

### Field 05 expansion — Action block

Commands list owner, prerequisites, acceptance, refusal, timeout, partial result, rollback display, and closure receipt.

### Field 06 expansion — Public wording block

Notices separate short status, long explanation, pending decision, public scope, correction line, and accessibility label. Private requester text is never concatenated into a public notice without permission.

### Field 07 expansion — Labor/privacy block

Worker names, requester names, and witness accounts have separate visibility scopes. Roster and consent owners can narrow them at runtime.

### Field 08 expansion — Save block

The row points to owner project, material, labor, and notice receipts. It declares migration behavior without adding a civic save section.

### Field 09 expansion — Determinism block

Seeded volunteer selection, tie breaks, and notice ordering name explicit streams and stable IDs.

### Field 10 expansion — Migration block

Old request key, new key, preserved receipts, public-record behavior, package version, and rollback note are mandatory for changes.

## Pass 57 — Public service desk UI, participation access, and correction literacy

This pass specifies the player-facing civic desk.

### Field 01 expansion — Intake board

The board shows request source, evidence class, site, age, owner, and preferred channel. It does not expose private detail in the summary row.

### Field 02 expansion — Priority explanation

Priority reasons are visible as urgency, dependency, safety, reach, or capacity facts. The player can inspect the contributing owner responses.

### Field 03 expansion — Project panel

The project panel shows materials, labor, route, weather window, owner state, and next command. A missing fact disables only the dependent command.

### Field 04 expansion — Participation panel

Residents can submit a report, volunteer, refuse, ask for an interpreter, request a separate statement, or choose a quiet update channel.

### Field 05 expansion — Notice panel

Notices separate confirmed work, pending work, rejected work, and corrected work. Original and revised text are linked.

### Field 06 expansion — Accessibility panel

Focus order reaches filters, evidence, owner status, next action, history, and correction. Visual and text equivalents remain available in quiet mode.

### Field 07 expansion — Regional panel

A regional relay shows destination, route, acknowledgment, and expected update. It does not copy mutable project state from another region.

### Field 08 expansion — Archive drawer

Archive shows source, retention, privacy scope, correction chain, and project receipt. It loads on demand.

### Field 09 expansion — Interruption recovery

Closing and reopening restores selected request, focus, last notice, and pending action without replaying the same alert.

### Field 10 expansion — Error language

Errors state whether the owner lacks evidence, labor, material, route, consent, or capacity. Technical details stay in diagnostics.

## Pass 58 — Civic performance envelope, service lifecycle, and stress fixtures

This pass bounds the public desk under large request volume.

### Field 01 expansion — Indexed intake

Index status, site, region, category, evidence, age, and owner. Load detail only for the selected request.

### Field 02 expansion — Owner subscription budget

Subscribe visible project detail to relevant owner events. Hidden requests update through bounded adapters.

### Field 03 expansion — Material paging

Material history and delivery receipts page by cursor. Do not load every inventory line for a request board.

### Field 04 expansion — Notice paging

Public notices and corrections use summary-first paging and stable source keys.

### Field 05 expansion — Regional refresh

Route, weather, colony, and capacity refresh on owner event, explicit refresh, or bounded timer.

### Field 06 expansion — Alert coalescing

Routine project and meeting updates coalesce. Water safety, structural, route, and power emergencies bypass routine grouping with duplicate keys.

### Field 07 expansion — Save workload

Save request references, owner receipts, notice keys, and correction keys, not duplicated project or inventory state.

### Field 08 expansion — Lifecycle release

Closing detail releases notices, images, and material lists while keeping selected request and focus target.

### Field 09 expansion — Failure isolation

A malformed optional civic row fails that row/package and preserves base project routes and public history.

### Field 10 expansion — Evidence report

Record fixture volume, detail calls, subscriptions, notice pages, save/restore timing, and alert counts.

## Pass 60 — Civic governance, equitable service, and long-horizon maintenance health

This pass sets post-release review rules for a large public-works library.

### Field 01 expansion — Evidence freshness

Open requests show source age and refresh event. Stale evidence offers review, not an invented status.

### Field 02 expansion — Participation equity

Review samples check alternate channels, mobility, language, quiet hours, and private statements through owner facts.

### Field 03 expansion — Material fairness

Partial deliveries and reservations remain visible. A project cannot appear complete while the material owner is waiting.

### Field 04 expansion — Labor dignity

Refusal, substitution, rest, and training remain valid outcomes and are never hidden in a priority score.

### Field 05 expansion — Public correction

Corrections preserve original and revised notices with source links and affected project references.

### Field 06 expansion — Seasonal maintenance

Weather and winter phase re-evaluate only projects affected by an owner event and explain the new window.

### Field 07 expansion — Package retirement

Retired civic stories leave legacy requests and project receipts without dangling actions.

### Field 08 expansion — Writer diagnostics

Diagnostics find repeated fallback, unsupported site IDs, stale copy, private text leaks, and duplicate request keys.

### Field 09 expansion — Release claims

Store and onboarding claims use verified project, water, press, and accessibility evidence only.

### Field 10 expansion — Sampling

Quarterly review samples submitted, waiting, active, refused, corrected, completed, reopened, private, and legacy requests.

## Pass 61 — Water and service operations, evidence ladders, and public trust

A resident, research owner, treatment owner, shelter, or route owner supplies the initial request and timestamp.

The responsible water or research owner supplies sample, quantity, quality, and confidence. The civic board does not create a source registry.

Fluid delivery and inventory owners confirm delivery, reservation, or failure.

### Field 07 — Public wording
Notices distinguish safe, pending, restricted, sampled, and unknown.

### Field 08 — Access
Residents can receive a board, radio, teacher, courier, or assisted update.

### Field 09 — Correction
New samples and treatment results link to the prior notice.

### Field 10 — Closure
The request closes with owner receipt, notice, source, and next review.

## Pass 114 — Fields 11–20 after the 100k gate

The civic plan now receives its second field layer. These fields extend maintenance and public decision making with evidence provenance, safety policy, volunteer support, accessibility, observability, and long-tail stewardship. They remain owner-bound proposals and do not create a parallel civic ledger, water authority, project scheduler, or reputation store.

### Field 11 — Work-order provenance

Every public repair, inspection, and completion claim needs a provenance label. A label can identify a resident request, a survey result, a maintenance owner, an emergency event, or an authored historical record. The label is review metadata attached to an existing project or settlement fact. It does not grant a panel permission to invent completion. Provenance survives a save round trip when the underlying project survives and disappears with temporary observations when their owner expires them. A same-seed fixture checks stable ordering, source display, and missing-source behavior.

### Field 12 — Public safety policy cards

Safety cards explain restrictions before a player accepts a civic job. A card may describe a load limit, a contamination boundary, a night-work rule, or an escort requirement. Records use stable IDs, explicit severity, prerequisite, explanation, and failure text. The host presents the card and routes the command; the project, water, travel, or inventory owner validates it. An unavailable policy produces a reason and a recovery action. Migration maps absent fields to conservative defaults and reports invalid references during catalog validation.

### Field 13 — Inspection notebook tooling

Inspectors need a structured notebook for measurements, photographs represented as asset IDs, witness names, and follow-up recommendations. The notebook points to existing locations and projects and never becomes a second completion ledger. Entries have unreviewed, confirmed, contradicted, and archived states. A review command either promotes a fact through the current owner or leaves the note as evidence. The UI supports filters and a compact mobile view. Save tests cover partial writes, duplicate observations, and a promoted entry restored after a restart.

### Field 14 — Maintenance policy rotation

Maintenance windows shift with thaw, storm, harvest, and shelter demand. An authored schedule supplies the active policy ID and next transition through the established calendar owner. Runtime decisions use the deterministic session clock and emit one refresh event when a boundary is crossed. A restored save recomputes the active schedule from saved time rather than local wall clock. The panel shows current, upcoming, and superseded policies so a player understands why a familiar task is temporarily unavailable.

### Field 15 — Public deliberation record

A civic choice can require a meeting, a vote, or a recorded objection. The record stores participants, scope, options presented, decision, dissent summary, and expiration condition. It is a campaign or relationship fact only when a current owner supports that authority; otherwise it remains an authored prompt awaiting a decision. Withdrawal or later amendment adds a new record without erasing history. UI copy distinguishes a proposal from an adopted action, and focused tests prove that merely opening a meeting does not mutate the settlement.

### Field 16 — Long-tail stewardship content

Completed work should continue to produce small, meaningful observations: a repaired path needs clearing, a shared tool is missing, a child adds a marker, or a rainstorm reveals a weak edge. Each entry declares location, repeat policy, prerequisite, consequence owner, and a quiet presentation option. Content review rejects entries that merely restate a completed project. A long-tail bank supports seasonal, once-only, and replayable records while preserving deterministic selection and clear follow-up routes.

### Field 17 — Civic service telemetry

Telemetry records bounded facts useful for tuning: queued work, blocked commands, completion time, event fan-out, panel refreshes, save size, and abandoned inspections. It excludes private free text and remains a read-only consumer. Sampling and event names live with the existing owner. A fixture compares state hashes with telemetry enabled and disabled, then checks allocation and refresh budgets for a full settlement roster. Any gameplay difference blocks rollout because instrumentation must not become a hidden project authority.

### Field 18 — Public works accessibility mode

An accessibility mode replaces animated progress and color-only status with persistent labels, icons, a text timeline, and inspectable reasons. It changes presentation only; project, water, travel, and inventory calculations remain unchanged. Controller users reach the same detail route as pointer users, and reduced-motion mode avoids repeated screen movement. Acceptance covers high contrast, focus visibility, large text, long translated labels, keyboard-only completion, and a clear recovery message after an invalid civic command.

### Field 19 — Civic archive export

At a settlement milestone, the player can review a compact archive of repaired paths, water notices, public decisions, unresolved requests, and stewardship notes. The archive reads stable facts in deterministic order and remains available after reload. It is not a new save store and never gates active play. If exported, the versioned format omits private notes and reports missing references visibly. Acceptance includes an identical-seed checksum, an old archive read, a missing-record fixture, and a clear statement of which facts were excluded.

### Field 20 — Civic handoff matrix

The integrator receives a matrix linking every civic field to its owner, catalog record, event, save section, UI route, focused test, performance fixture, accessibility case, and rollback instruction. Blank cells identify design-only work or an architecture blocker. The matrix is reviewed after every implementation slice and stored with the handoff. It prevents plan volume from being treated as integration evidence and gives future work a bounded starting point. Closure requires current source proof, an observable host route, and a clean rollback path.

## Wave 35 integration closeout receipt — Plan 3: Common Ground: Community Public Works

**Closeout status:** documentation-only; READY FOR PREMISE AUDIT. This receipt does not claim implementation.

**Program role:** water, projects, settlement, territory, colony, reputation, press, archive, and civic labor

**Primary owners:** water treatment, fluid delivery, project, territory, settlement, colony, reputation, press, and archive owners

**Required delta:** a public-work request and result projection that consumes existing water, project, or settlement facts without creating a civic ledger or duplicate completion counter

**First safe slice:** one maintenance request for a current water or shelter asset with inspect, assign, defer, refuse, and completed-result callbacks

**Evidence anchors:** a chalked intake valve, a patched bridge plank, a bucket tally, and a public notice pinned under glass

**Observable signals:** flow confidence, work age, crew availability, public trust, repair risk, and service callback

### Closeout boundary

The plan closes at the design boundary where one current owner can publish a fact, one consumer can display or consume it, one command can be issued through the owner, and one recovery path can return the player to a known state. The plan does not create a second ledger, registry, cache authority, save store, event bus, or presentation-owned counter. A row remains design-only until a current source search proves its consumer.

### Integration contract

The first receipt must identify the owner, public API, data file, save section or stateless proof, host route, focused tests, and rollback. It must exercise source age, stale input, duplicate delivery, interruption, correction, keyboard/controller parity, empty and error states, and one delayed content callback. The same seed and ordered inputs must reproduce the result across save, reload, host reopen, and duplicate event delivery.

### Content and failure gate

The first content slice uses pump repairs, bridge crews, neighborhood disputes, public notices, resource tradeoffs, and reputation callbacks. It includes discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, choice, quiet success, costly success, refusal, unresolved outcome, delayed callback, repeat policy, and retirement rule. It must stop safely for second project authority, false completion, water-source duplication, reputation writes from prose, and unbounded worker queues. Prose can describe evidence and uncertainty but cannot create a gameplay fact.

### Handoff

**MUST PRESERVE:** existing authority, engine-free Core, JSON data authority, deterministic ordering, current save ownership, truthful UI, and active path claims.

**MUST ADD:** one premise receipt, one owner-bound slice, one validator-backed sample, one replay or stateless proof, one accessible route, one focused verification result, and one rollback note.

**MUST NOT DO:** duplicate state, revive retired architecture, claim runtime integration from document volume, or widen the catalog before reachability.

**NEXT ACTION:** run the bounded premise audit for the first safe slice and return the evidence to the integrator.
